note: 2 systems (figs_new/p100_s00.png, p100_s01.png). F major, one flat (Bb) in key sig applied throughout - no natural signs seen, so every bare B is Bb5. F is consistently raised via an explicit written sharp (#) at every occurrence - a chromatic raised-4th figure, cross-checked in zoomed crops. Each phrase = 3 beamed 8th notes followed by a fermata over an 8th rest (r:8^), 13 phrases total across the 2 systems (6 in s00, 7 in s01), matching the 'triplets w/ fermatas' note. No literal triplet '3' numeral is visible above any beam group despite the catalog description calling them triplets - they are plain groups of 3 beamed 8ths, so encoded without a triplet marker. All pitches and durations cross-checked against 4x/8x zoom crops.

No pitch, rhythm only, rit. & dim. Staffless monotone row (figs_new/p102_s00b.png): 17 note-glyphs on a single line with no staff, marked 'f' at the start and 'Rit. & dim.' partway through. Careful pixel-level comparison of the note glyphs shows the first 11 have a double flag (16th notes, tight/even spacing ~50px) and the remaining 6 switch to a single flag (8th notes, wider spacing ~62px) with a small staccato dot added above each - i.e. the ritardando is written out as literally longer note values plus wider spacing, and the diminuendo as staccato dots, rather than any gradual/continuous ramp. Encoded on an arbitrary single pitch (C5) throughout since there is no staff or pitch information. Staccato dots on the second half are not representable in the pitch:dur format and are only noted here.

Accent marks ('>') appear over many notes throughout and staccato dots appear on the decay-row tails; neither is representable in the pitch:dur format and both are omitted from the encoding (noted here instead). Several duration/voicing judgment calls (dropped chord tones, quarter-vs-eighth reads on unflagged stems, decay-row tail values) keep the overall confidence at 'med' even though most pitches and beam groupings were cross-checked closely against 8-10x zoom crops and, where ambiguous, against connected-component pixel analysis of notehead positions.
